chapter: Touring, recording and Fletcher's band in the 1940s
title: Studio technique in the 1930s: mikes, pre-rehearsal and relaxed sessions
summary: Mikes were hung over groups; arrangements were rehearsed beforehand because studio time was paid by the hour, and groovy tunes made relaxed sessions.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: The other day, we talked a little bit about recording, and we were talking mainly about your first recording experience back in the mid-twenties, and then a while ago we were talking about the records you made with your band and with Fletcher's in -- towards the late thirties, and I just be sort of interested in what -- was there much change in the technique -- recording techniques, and the way they set the band up, and such things as that?
Well, let's see. If I remember correctly, we're talking about the era of Christopher Columbus.
Did they use separate microphones for each group?
Yeah. They had mikes suspended over the artists, and you know, having recorded then and the way they do now, it's quite a bit different.
Oh yeah. Generally, before you went to record something, did you have it pretty well rehearsed, or did you go into the studio and then rehearse the arrangement?

No, they would rehearse before the band got to the studio, because I think, Tom, the sessions at that time, they had to -- they were paying union scale or something by the hour, and if you hadn't rehearsed the arrangement before you got there, and had to clean up things, this was on the man's time, so they say, and so they kind of used to beef on that. So usually, the arrangements were pretty well rehearsed before they got there, and the only thing that

might happen in rehearsal, the time element might have been a factor. They might have had to either extend it or cut something out, and that way, after the arrangement naturally had been made, with a big group, you've got to mark the arrangement, where to cut, and what to leave out, you know, and where to come back in again. That might take up a little time, which -- they allowed for that, but as far as getting the arrangement down so it'd be smooth, no way.
Were the recording sessions pretty businesslike, or did you still have a lot of fun, pretty relaxed, or what was the general atmosphere?
Yeah. The band was relaxed, especially if the tunes that they were gonna record were groovy things, you know.

Excuse me. Then you wouldn't mind really blowing. Some of the -- some great things were played during that time, cause you get the beat, and if the set up, again, like you said before, if it was correct, you could hear everything, the rhythm and all, then you'd get a good sound. Some of those old 78's prove that, you know.
